adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent`, the diff changes `selectedCalendar` to:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

The `.find(...)` branch is only executed when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (e.g., `undefined`/`null`/""), but the predicate compares each `cal.externalId` to that same falsy `externalCalendarId`. In normal data, calendar `externalId` values are non-falsy strings, so this comparison will not match and the expression resolves to `undefined`. That makes the fallback lookup ineffective (it can’t select a calendar when `externalCalendarId` isn’t provided). The same flawed pattern is also introduced in `deleteEvent` later in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, deleteEvent sets `const calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is not provided (undefined/null), the fallback `.find(...)` compares each `cal.externalId` to that same undefined value, so it will almost always return `undefined` and thus not select any destination calendar. Given the surrounding code defines `defaultCalendarId = "primary"`, the delete will end up targeting the primary calendar instead of the intended destination calendar when `externalCalendarId` is missing. This is a concrete logic bug introduced in the diff.
